not_verified: Other modules' tests that pin /8 as the format in force now fail with R35's /10 and need restating by their own jobs: case-authoring 4 (document.test R14/R55, R14 x2, R17), case-catalogue 2 (checks.test R1/R3/R4, R1/R4 N538), publication 1 (K651 re-export, expects /8); all green at tranche. case-checker's program.mjs embeds this module and must be regenerated by its own build (its 4 reds, R2/R8/R19 G50, R13 x2, R25, fail at tranche too). R38 says a document with no extract keeps /8 or /9; I followed R35 (caseDocumentFormatFor answers /10 always) and the stored goldens re-render byte for byte. R38's list fields (kept_columns, roles, dropped_columns, header, row) are written as R17 writes lists (canonical JSON in one quoted value), not the grammar's inline list, which cuts a cell at a comma. materialsOf adds extract only on a row stating an extract field, so every other row reads exactly as before (others' tests deepEqual those rows). R39's control that removing a limit makes case-checker R30 fail is not run: case-checker R30 is not yet built; the test shows the limit-less extract reads use_limit null. The typedStepOf edge (Uses, text-chain) was not added: the block takes rows its author derives, and modules.json is BOB's. R14 does not yet print a register extract's own lines (not asked by R38).

exempt.revert: Two new tests are pins that pass on the old code by design: t53 'R35 control: a stored /8 and /9 case file re-render byte for byte' (the digests were recorded from the code before the change) and notice-strength-176's second test (confirms R14 item 8 prints strength's bio-grading/5 rule with no code change here).
